elements.element: Customer owns deliverables/work product created for it, with express Vendor assignment
elements.evidence: "Garman hereby assigns to Sparkling all intellectual property rights in the Modifications and any other deliverables developed for Sparkling"
"Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements thereto)"

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: "grants Sparkling a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence ... any Garman intellectual property embedded in or required to use those Modifications and deliverables"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: "Nothing in this Agreement transfers to Garman any right, title or interest in Sparkling's data ... remains the property of Sparkling"
"No intellectual property created under this Agreement shall be jointly owned."

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: Only "Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work"; no reference to generic tools or know-how

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for Customer's business
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense ... for the purposes of Sparkling's business"

reasons: All five atomic preferred elements are present in operative text: assignment of deliverables/Modifications, Vendor retention of the Work, an embedded-IP licence back, Customer Data retention, and an anti-joint-ownership statement, so the locked preferred level is complete.
Fallback is incomplete as a standalone bargain (no express Vendor ownership of generic tools and know-how), but that is irrelevant given the preferred level is satisfied.

Minimality fails: the edit imports fallback-only rights ("worldwide", "modify and sublicense") into a preferred proposal, adds an unnecessary "notwithstanding Section 3" cross-reference and a "required to use" expansion, and rewrites a 49-word sentence into 163 words (3.33x expansion; 0.743 changed-character ratio) where a tighter assignment/licence insertion appended to the existing anchor would suffice.
Narrowing the assignment to deliverables "paid for by Sparkling" adds a condition beyond the playbook's "created for it" scope; note in rationale rather than expand further.

Intent is preserved: Garman's platform ownership, the Section 2 location-limited licence, the sublicensing restriction in (c) and the additional-fee mechanic remain effective, and the new "Except as expressly provided in this Section 13" carve-out avoids contradiction with the no-transfer sentence.
